# Unit Tests for English: Test Requirements Quality

**Purpose**: Validate the quality, clarity, and completeness of test requirements for unit and integration tests in the Quantity Calculation feature.
**Created**: 2026-09-19
**Feature**: [Quantity Calculation](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Are unit test requirements explicitly defined for all Rust modules (e.g., `quantity/`, `ui/`, `config/`)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK002 - Are integration test requirements specified for CLI/TUI interfaces? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK003 - Are test coverage requirements quantified with specific thresholds (e.g., 80% coverage for critical paths)? [Clarity, Spec §NFR-1]
- [x] CHK004 - Are test requirements defined for all error paths and failure modes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK005 - Is the term "sensible" quantified with specific criteria for test inclusion/exclusion? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK006 - Are test failure scenarios explicitly defined for all error paths (e.g., invalid inputs, file I/O errors)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK007 - Are test success criteria measurable (e.g., "all tests pass", "coverage > 80%")? [Measurability, Spec §NFR-1]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK008 - Are test requirements consistent between Rust modules and CLI/TUI interfaces? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK009 - Do test requirements align with the project's error handling strategy (e.g., `thiserror` usage)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK010 - Are acceptance criteria for test cases explicitly defined (e.g., "test passes if quantity calculation matches expected output")? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK011 - Can test success/failure be objectively measured? [Measurability, Spec §NFR-1]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK012 - Are alternate test scenarios (e.g., partial failures, edge cases) addressed in requirements? [Coverage, Gap]
- [x] CHK013 - Are recovery test scenarios (e.g., rollback, state restoration) defined for state mutations? [Coverage, Gap]
- [x] CHK014 - Are test requirements defined for zero-state scenarios (e.g., empty packing list)? [Coverage, Edge Case]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK015 - Are edge cases for invalid inputs (e.g., negative weekdays, invalid travel style) addressed in test requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK016 - Are edge cases for conflicting inputs (e.g., hot weather + snowboarding) addressed in test requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-006]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK017 - Are performance test requirements defined for quantity calculation operations (e.g., <500ms)? [Coverage, Spec §NFR-2]
- [x] CHK018 - Are stress test requirements defined for high-load scenarios (e.g., 1000+ items)? [Coverage, Spec §NFR-3]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK019 - Are external dependency test requirements documented (e.g., config file loading, `.config/pack-liste/` directory)? [Dependency, Gap]
- [x] CHK020 - Are test requirements aligned with the project's error handling strategy (e.g., `thiserror` usage)? [Assumption, Spec §FR-006]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK021 - Is the exclusion of UI testing explicitly documented as intentional? [Assumption, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK022 - Are there any conflicts between test requirements and error handling requirements? [Conflict]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`.
